info.label: Info commands
info.description: Utility commands: info about a member, the server, a role, or someone's avatar.

opt.emoji: The emoji to enlarge (custom, :name: or unicode).

avatar.description: Show a member's avatar in full size.
avatar.title: {user}'s avatar

emoji.description: Show an emoji in full size (downloadable).
emoji.notEmoji: ❌ That's not a valid emoji. Provide a custom emoji, a server `:name:`, or a unicode emoji.

g0.label: 🪪 Profile log
g0.description: Records members' identity changes in a channel (name, profile picture, server nickname). The /userinfo, /serverinfo… commands stay available at all times.

watchEnabled.label: Enable the profile log
watchEnabled.help: Turns on the identity-change log. The information commands (`/infos-membre`…) work independently: this setting is not about turning those off.

watchChannelId.label: Log channel
watchChannelId.help: The channel changes are logged to. Empty, nothing is written even with watching on. Keep it staff-only: everybody's former names scroll past in it.

watchUsername.label: Username (@handle)
watchUsername.help: The global, unique Discord @handle. It is the one that matters for spotting a returning account: it rarely changes, and rarely without a reason.

watchGlobalName.label: Display name
watchGlobalName.help: The account's display name, used across all of Discord. Changes often and harmlessly — this is the box that fills the log the most for the least information.

watchAvatar.label: Profile picture
watchAvatar.help: The profile picture. The log keeps a link to the old image: Discord removes it from its servers after a while, and the link eventually shows nothing.

watchNickname.label: Server nickname
watchNickname.help: The nickname specific to THIS server. It is the one moderation itself changes to clean up an unreadable name — expect to see your own actions in the log.

watchRoleIds.label: Limit to these roles (empty = every member)
watchRoleIds.help: Restricts watching to members holding one of these roles. Empty, everyone is watched. On a large server, sticking to sensitive roles avoids an unreadable log where the one notable change gets lost.
